story.title: Tidal Lock (The Jovian Ledger, Book One)
story.premise: In 2214, Piq Varga is a covert loss adjuster for Lagrange Mutual, the insurance society that underwrites nearly every cargo moving through the outer solar system. Whoever insures the ships knows where they all are, so Lagrange's Special Losses division works as a private intelligence service. Piq is sent to Asgard Yard on Callisto under a genuine credential as a mass auditor. Her job is to find out where 340 tonnes of water ice went and what an intercepted line means: 'throw before conjunction, no one will see it until it's done.' Her handler fears a weapon launch or an engineered insurance fraud, and Jupiter's solar conjunction will cut her off from him in 38 days. Then Piq realizes the faint pulses she has been tracing are coming from the deadly surface of Europa, not from a cabal on Callisto. The tug Ninefold Grace was declared lost with all hands fourteen months ago, and four of its crew are alive, buried in the ice with a failing reactor. Piq has to choose between her employer and the truth. She has to outmaneuver a security chief who needs those survivors to stay dead, and she has to work out a delta-v and radiation budget that does not close. Through all of it she falls slowly and against her own instincts for Teodora Anand, the station's dose warden, who despises insurers, rations every sievert, and whose sister is one of the voices under the ice.
story.setting:
The Jupiter system in 2214. Humans have settled the outer planets without faster-than-light travel or communication. Earth and Luna (the Compact) and the Martian cooperatives compete for Jovian water, which serves as propellant, shielding and air.

Asgard Yard: a station of about 1,900 people buried under regolith in the Valhalla impact basin on Callisto's leading hemisphere. Surface gravity is 0.126 g. Callisto is tidally locked, so a local day lasts 16.7 Earth days and Jupiter hangs fixed and low in the sky. Callisto sits outside Jupiter's main radiation belts, so surface dose is a fraction of a millisievert a day. That makes it the only comfortable major moon.

The Sling: Asgard's 40 km electromagnetic mass driver, which throws shelled ice slugs toward inner-system customers on multi-year trajectories.

Ganymede: Ur Station, a Martian-aligned rival with its own weak magnetosphere and a dose of about 0.08 Sv per day.

Europa: about 5 Sv per day on its trailing hemisphere. That is lethal within a day for an unshielded person, but survivable under meters of ice.

Comms with Earth-Luna take 45 to 52 minutes one way. As Jupiter approaches solar conjunction, traffic is rerouted through a store-and-forward relay at Mars. The relay batches messages, reorders them by priority and size, and then goes dark entirely for 19 days.

Physical constraints that drive the plot:
- Every kilogram is logged, taxed and weighed.
- Oxygen comes from electrolyzed ice.
- Launch windows follow moon phasing: Europa's synodic period as seen from Callisto is about 4.5 days.
- Moving mass costs propellant on an exponential curve.
- Water is simultaneously propellant, shielding and life.
story.tone:
Instructions for every chapter:

Viewpoint and prose:
- Close third person on Piq throughout. The reader knows only what she perceives, counts and infers, and her auditor's mind colors the narration: she weighs, tallies and reconciles everything, including feelings she refuses to name.
- Prose is vivid but economical. Use concrete sensory detail of low-g life (the slow arc of dropped objects, regolith grit in seals, the ozone tang of electrolysis, Jupiter's banded light on frost) and no purple passages. Prefer one precise image to three adjectives.
- Each chapter runs about 4,000 to 5,000 words.
- Every chapter ends with forward momentum: a new fact, a decision, a threat, a message arriving, or a countdown advancing. Never close on a comfortable pause.

Hard science:
- The physics is a felt constraint on choices, not a lecture.
- Light delay, dose numbers, delta-v and mass budgets appear as stakes that characters argue about, joke about and bleed for.

Suspense:
- Spycraft is tight and procedural. Clocks are explicit: conjunction, reactor drum life, launch windows.

Comedy:
- Comedy is regular and situational. It grows from:
  - mass bureaucracy;
  - overlapping cover duties;
  - the light-delay absurdities of out-of-order messages;
  - low-g and microgravity mishaps;
  - a contraband cat;
  - a cross-moon wedding with a three-second vow delay.
- Humor stays dry and character-driven. It drops away completely during the tensest sequences: the interrogation, the Europa surface, the jettison and the rendezvous. It returns only once a crisis has broken.

Romance:
- The slow burn is built through competence and friction: dose consultations, shared calculations, near-touches interrupted by procedure.
- Teo is never an enemy agent and never betrays Piq, even when she is furious with her.
- The emotional register is wry, warm, morally serious and quietly aching.

characters.name: Piq Varga
characters.role: Protagonist. Special Losses adjuster (spy) for Lagrange Mutual. Undercover as a certified mass auditor and notary on Asgard Yard. She was raised on a cycler ship by a weigh-master father and genuinely holds her cover credential.
characters.want: To close the file cleanly and balance the ledger. She wants to earn the senior partnership that would let her stop living out of a 20 kg mass allowance, and, beneath that, to belong somewhere that will not reprice her.
characters.flaw: She converts people into line items and intimacy into risk assessment. She lies easily by omission and trusts her own numbers so completely that she assumes the world, including her handler, is working from the same ledger she is.

characters.name: Teodora 'Teo' Anand
characters.role: Love interest. Asgard's dose warden, the radiation health officer who sets and enforces every resident's sievert budget and can ground anyone. Older sister of Amaya, an engineer lost with the Ninefold Grace.
characters.want: To learn what really happened to the Ninefold Grace and force Lagrange Mutual to admit fault for denying the claim. Above all, to keep everyone under their dose limit, because rules are the only thing that has never lied to her.
characters.flaw: She uses rigid rule-keeping as armor against grief. She holds contempt for insurers as a class, and she would rather carry everything alone than ask for help or admit she is afraid.

characters.name: Augustin Pell
characters.role: Piq's handler at Lagrange Mutual's Earth-Moon L4 headquarters, 45 to 52 light-minutes away. Terse, old-school and actuarial.
characters.want: To protect the society's solvency and his adjusters, in that order. Slowly he learns to want to reverse that order.
characters.flaw: He trusts models over people. He writes orders so compressed that they read colder than he means them, which is lethal when each message is a week stale.

characters.name: Hesper Okafor-Lund
characters.role: Chief engineer of the Sling and quiet leader of the Bucket Brigade, the station workers secretly diverting ice to fit out a rescue tug.
characters.want: To bring the Ninefold Grace crew home, whom she trained.
characters.flaw: She has a martyr's recklessness. She plans to fly the rescue herself even though she is the only person who can keep the depot running.

characters.name: Dov 'Lucky' Mbeki
characters.role: Tug pilot of the patched-together rescue tug Mule. Comic relief with real nerve. About to marry Ziva, a tanker pilot from Ur Station, over a three-second light-delay link.
characters.want: To fly something that matters, and to meet his fiancée in the same room.
characters.flaw: He talks constantly, gambles on superstition, and leaks secrets through sheer enthusiasm.

characters.name: Marek Saar
characters.role: Antagonist. Head of security for the Jovian Development Authority (JDA) on Asgard. He openly opposes Piq's snooping and the Brigade.
characters.want: To keep the Ninefold Grace officially dead. He signed the ruling that dismissed its distress pulses as an automated echo. Live survivors would mean liability for the JDA and ruin for him.
characters.flaw: He has absolute certainty and a talent for cruelty dressed as protocol. His own rules can be used against him.

characters.name: Director Ilse Rook
characters.want: To keep the colony insured, supplied and solvent through a bad repricing year.
characters.flaw: Cowardice disguised as prudence. She has hidden a failing depot sunshade and the ice it is costing rather than trigger a rate hike.

characters.name: Amaya Anand
characters.role: Engineer of the Ninefold Grace and Teo's younger sister. She is the voice in the pulses from Europa, keying messages in the dosimetry protocol Teo taught her.
characters.want: To keep her three surviving crewmates alive until someone believes them.
characters.flaw: Stubborn, almost reckless optimism. She will spend her own dose to save a sample or a person.

characters.name: Commissioner Yusuf Haddad-Ferreira
characters.role: Head of Ur Station on Ganymede. Martian-aligned and publicly framed by the JDA as a threat.
characters.want: To mount a rescue without being accused of an act of war in the JDA's claimed Europa zone.
characters.flaw: He is secretive to the point of paralysis and speaks only in diplomatic protocol, so his signals are misread as hostility.

characters.name: Ziva Kalnins
characters.role: Pilot of the Ur propellant tanker Steadfast Margin and Lucky's fiancée.
characters.want: To finally be in the same room as Lucky, and to bring the tanker home full of people instead of fuel.
characters.flaw: Deadpan to the point of being unreadable. She is also Haddad's most loyal subordinate, which makes her careful about what she says on open channels.

characters.name: Ballast
characters.role: A contraband 4.1 kg tabby cat living in Asgard's ventilation system. A recurring comic subplot and an unwitting interrupter of romantic moments.
characters.flaw: Has never once been declared on a manifest.

story.arc:
STRUCTURE: 24 chapters in three acts, about 4,000 to 5,000 words each. There are four major twists plus one supporting reveal. None is a betrayal, and none involves anyone lying about who they are. Every clue is planted at least two chapters before its reveal.

ACT ONE: THE AUDIT (Chapters 1 to 8)

Ch 1, Weigh-In.
- Piq descends to Callisto and is 1.3 kg over her mass allowance because of the Lagrange spy kit.
- Comedy: she talks her way through by declaring the hollow comms unit as 'audit reference masses'.
- At dose intake she meets Teo, who refuses her a dosimeter waiver and calls auditors and insurers 'the same species of vulture'. The spark is immediate and hostile.
- Through the shuttle port Piq notices frost on the sunward face of the ice depot, which is physically wrong. [Clue for the sublimation reveal.]
- She reviews Pell's briefing: the 'throw before conjunction' fragment reached Lagrange through a commercial intercept broker. [Seeds hook 2.]
- Ending: on her first night inside the depot ledger she finds the 340-tonne gap.

Ch 2, The Ledger.
- Piq begins her real audit job and recites Lagrange's Clause 14(c), the dose clause, to a grumbling tug crew. The clause mandates minimum shielding water on any Europa-bound vessel. [T2 clue.]
- A comms tech explains the Mars relay, which batches traffic and deprioritizes large padded packets as conjunction nears. [T3 clue.]
- Saar introduces himself with a smile that audits her back.
- Hesper gives her a tour of the Sling.
- Comedy: residents hide mass everywhere. Piq's sensor sweep flags a 4.1 kg anomaly in a duct, and it is Ballast the cat.
- Ending: her covert receiver catches a pulse on a retired dosimetry maintenance band.

Ch 3, Pattern.
- Piq logs the pulses. They go silent for about 30 hours every 4.5 days, which she reads as a cabal's shift roster. [T1 clue.]
- Cover collision: Ibis Metrology has also listed her as a notary, and the station asks her to officiate a cross-moon wedding.
- Ending: she tails Hesper to a sealed hangar and sees a decommissioned tug, the Mule, being wrapped in ice blocks.

Ch 4, Mule.
- Piq stakes out the hangar.
- Lucky complains that 'Lagrange's water blankets cost me 300 meters per second' on every Europa job. [T2 clue.]
- Tracking shows an Ur tanker loitering in a Ganymede-Callisto transfer orbit, which the JDA calls provocation. [T4 clue.]
- Comedy: a low-g pursuit through a hydroponics gallery ends with Piq bouncing helplessly into a lettuce rack.
- Ending: Saar catches her outside the hangar and says, 'Auditors who wander get audited.'

Ch 5, The Dome.
- Piq's dose has ticked up from standing near the Mule's reactor, so Teo summons her for a consultation. The scene is funny, prickly and charged.
- At the viewing dome Teo explains that Europa 'ducks behind the old man' every four and a half days and that the dosimeters sing differently when it does. [T1 clue.]
- Teo mentions her lost sister.
- Ending: a 49-minute-old order from Pell arrives: identify the throw cabal and treat the depot crew as hostile.

Ch 6, Vows.
- Comedy set piece: Piq officiates Lucky's wedding to Ziva over a link to the Ur tanker. The three-second delay makes their vows overlap and collide.
- Pell's latest reply earnestly answers Piq's week-old question about how to log a cat. [T3 clue.]
- Piq notices a slow frequency drift in the pulses and blames cheap hardware. [T1 clue.]
- Ending: the wedding feed shows the Ur tanker carrying far more propellant than any routine run needs. [T4 clue.]

Ch 7, Sister.
- Teo shows Piq her sister Amaya's last dose log, which ends in an inexplicable spike. [T2 clue.]
- Piq finds that Rook cut the maintenance budget for the depot sunshade. [Sublimation clue.]
- The two women nearly touch hands over the data, then don't.
- Ending: Hesper corners Piq and asks, 'What are you really weighing?'

Ch 8, Echo. [TWIST 1, misread signal.]
- Piq overlays the silent gaps on Europa's occultations behind Jupiter. They match exactly.
- The frequency drift is the Doppler shift of Europa's orbital motion.
- The transmitter is on Europa. The Brigade has been listening, not coordinating.
- Piq breaks cover far enough to bring the pulses to Teo. Teo recognizes her own old dosimetry keying protocol, in her sister's hand.
- A faint secondary modulation in the pulses goes unexplained. [Seeds hook 1.]
- Ending, the decoded text: FOUR ALIVE. REACTOR DRUM 60 DAYS. PLEASE.

ACT TWO: THE BRIGADE (Chapters 9 to 16)

Ch 9.
- Piq sends Lagrange a long report saying the crew is alive.
- A stale message from Pell arrives. It says Ur has bought war-risk cover over the JDA's claimed Europa zone and orders Piq to stop any unlicensed launch by 'any means'. [T4 clue. Seeds hook 3.]
- The Brigade accepts Piq as 'the auditor who can count'. She hides her Lagrange employment from Teo.
- Ending: Saar decrees that every movement of ice now needs a security countersignature.

Ch 10.
- Piq reads Lagrange's claim file on the Ninefold Grace. The denial rests on the pilot having 'deviated to a low-energy trajectory'. [T2 clue.]
- Pell's next message asks about the weapon cabal as though her report never arrived. [T3 clue.]
- Comedy: a microgravity trip to an orbital tank farm with Teo, including a tumbling propellant bladder and a wrestling match with a stuck valve.
- Ending: Piq's delta-v ledger shows the Mule will be 140 m/s short of returning to Callisto with survivors aboard.

Ch 11.
- The Brigade works through the night in the hangar.
- Piq's message queue shows 'ACK pending' on her reports, and she dismisses it. [T3 clue.]
- She notices that the Ur-standard codec used in the original intercepted fragment is the wrong one for a Lagrange source. [Seeds hook 2.]
- Residents complain about rising humidity in the depot. [Sublimation clue.]
- Piq and Teo nearly kiss in an airlock, and Ballast interrupts.
- Ending: Saar confiscates the Brigade's receiver. Only Piq's covert receiver still links Callisto to Europa.

Ch 12.
- Piq becomes the Brigade's only link to the survivors.
- Amaya writes that 'the ice talks at night'. [Seeds hook 1.]
- Lucky quips, 'Ganymede's the cheap seats, but Ur would shoot us.' [T4 clue.]
- Teo plans dose triage for a surface rescue.
- Ending: the survivors transmit the Ninefold Grace's flight recorder file.

Ch 13, Clause. [TWIST 2, a consequence nobody predicted.]
- The flight data shows the cause of the loss. Clause 14(c) required 18 tonnes of shielding water, which pushed the tug past its delta-v margin. That forced the slow, low-energy path that lingered in Europa's plasma torus. A dose spike then latched up the flight computer, and the crew crash-landed.
- The 'pilot error' that justified Lagrange's denial was caused by Lagrange's own rule, the same clause Piq recited as gospel in Chapter 2.
- Teo is incandescent with rage at the insurer, still not knowing Piq works for it.
- Ending: Piq decides to tell her.

Ch 14.
- Commissioner Haddad sends a stiff, protocol-heavy message to the dose warden asking for Europa surface dose protocols and proposing 'dose sharing'. [T4 clue. Seeds hook 3.]
- Comedy: the JDA and Ur exchange formal notices of escalating politeness.
- At the dome, Piq confesses that she is a Lagrange Special Losses adjuster.
- Ending: Teo walks away, saying, 'I won't burn you. I'm not you.'

Ch 15.
- Teo stays cold but professional and does not expose Piq.
- Saar interrogates Piq in a tense scene with no humor. Piq uses the 100-minute round trip to Earth as an alibi: her transmissions are routine audit uploads that he cannot verify before the window closes.
- Ending: Saar admits he signed the 'automated echo' ruling and cannot let the survivors exist.

Ch 16, Backlog. [TWIST 3, wrong assumption about time delay.]
- The Mars relay operator explains that Piq's large padded reports have been stuck in the queue behind priority traffic all along.
- Every hard-line order from Pell was answering a world in which her last delivered report described a weapon cabal.
- Nine delayed messages from Pell arrive, out of order. The last says the survivors' existence has reached him, that Lagrange's salvage clause can fund the rescue, and 'help them, you'll be alone for 19 days.'
- Piq realizes she has been arguing with a ghost of her own earlier report.
- Teo reads Pell's message and begins to thaw.
- Ending: the conjunction blackout begins, and Saar locks down all launches.

ACT THREE: LINE OF SIGHT (Chapters 17 to 24)

Ch 17. [Sublimation reveal, hidden physical constraint.]
- Piq's audit finds that 96 of the 340 missing tonnes sublimated off the depot because of the failed sunshade, which Rook concealed. The Brigade took 244 tonnes.
- Piq uses the finding as leverage to bring Rook over.
- Ending: Saar's team cuts the Mule's propellant feed.

Ch 18, Seal.
- Piq impounds the Mule under her mass-audit and notary seal. She means it only as a delay.
- Under JDA statute, impounded assets fall outside security jurisdiction, so Saar's own protocol locks him out. The plan works for the wrong reason.
- Hesper gives up her martyrdom to stay behind and manually hold the depot pumps.
- Ending: the window opens in nine hours, and the ledger is still 140 m/s short.

Ch 19, Cheap Seats. [TWIST 4, recontextualized threat and orbital constraint.]
- Piq overlays the tanker's propellant load, the war-risk purchase, Haddad's dose questions and the tanker's loitering orbit.
- Ur has been preparing its own rescue all along. It bought war-risk cover because landing in the JDA's claimed zone could be ruled an act of war under the Compact. Its tanker is staged on a Europa-Ganymede transfer.
- Europa to Ganymede costs less delta-v than Europa to Callisto, so returning to Ganymede closes the ledger.
- Piq calls Haddad openly. He denies sending the original fragment. [Seeds hook 2.]
- Teo will go as medic. Piq will go as mass master.
- Ending: launch.

Ch 20.
- The transit runs through rising dose, with Teo calculating everyone's budget minute by minute.
- In the shielded cabin the two women share a quiet, intimate exchange. There is no comedy.
- Piq's habit of cross-checking catches a corrupted Europa navigation file that Saar planted.
- Ending: they land 2 km from the target.

Ch 21.
- A shielded crawler crosses chaos terrain under 5 Sv per day.
- They find the survivors: Captain Rhee, Wierzbicki, Oduya and Amaya. The sisters reunite.
- The crevasse is closing. A hydrophone has recorded structured periodic sounds that are not tidal cracking. [Seeds hook 1.]
- Ending: with four survivors aboard, the Mule is too heavy for the rendezvous.

Ch 22, Jettison.
- Piq audits every kilogram aboard.
- She leaves behind her Lagrange comms unit, the last tie to her job.
- Amaya keeps a 0.8 kg ice core sample. The dead crewmembers return only as dog tags.
- Piq takes extra time on the EVA to spare Teo's dose.
- Ending: the burn comes up short, and the tanker has to dive deeper to meet them.

Ch 23.
- The rendezvous happens deep in the radiation field.
- The Mule docks with Ziva's tanker.
- Comedy returns only after the docking succeeds: Lucky and Ziva meet in person for the first time.
- In the medical bay, while both show early symptoms of radiation sickness, Piq and Teo confess their love.
- Ending: course for Ur Station.

Ch 24.
Resolution on Ur Station. Pell's message arrives after the blackout ends.
- Lagrange reverses the Ninefold Grace denial, pays the claim, rewrites Clause 14(c) and funds the rescue as salvage.
- Lagrange's salvage funding comes with legal amnesty for the Brigade.
- Rook detains Saar for a Compact inquiry using Piq's seal logs, then resigns.
- The depot sunshade is repaired.
- The Ur-JDA war-risk claim is never triggered.
- Piq resigns from Special Losses, and Pell accepts with a rare unclipped apology.
- Ballast is officially entered into the Asgard ledger as 'biological pest control, 4.1 kg'.
- Lucky and Ziva settle on Ur.
- Amaya's crew is home.

Piq and Teo choose each other. Their future is uncertain:
- both carry elevated lifetime dose and blood counts that need watching;
- Teo's license is under review for exceeding limits;
- Piq has no job and no home moon.
Teo logs her own overdose honestly, and Piq does not reconcile the feeling; she simply lets it stand.

The final page lands on the hooks below.

Deliberate trilogy hooks, left open on purpose:
(1) THE EUROPA SOUNDS. Amaya's ice core and the hydrophone recordings of structured periodic sound from the ocean beneath the ice. Seeded in Chapters 8, 12 and 21. Their nature stays unexplained.
(2) THE UNKNOWN SOURCE. Someone in the Jupiter system wanted Piq there. The original fragment reached Lagrange through an intercept broker using an Ur-standard codec, and Haddad denies sending it. Seeded in Chapters 1, 11 and 19. On the final page an unsigned message arrives on the old dosimetry band: 'Well counted.'
(3) THE COMPACT'S ANSWER. Ur's landing in the JDA's claimed Europa zone prompts the Compact to dispatch the enforcement vessel Integrity, 26 months out, and Piq is named as a witness. Seeded in Chapters 9, 14 and 19.
subplots: Romance (central): Piq and Teo move from hostile first contact at dose intake, through dose consultations and shared all-night calculations, to near-touches interrupted by procedure and Ballast. Piq's confession that she works for Lagrange (Ch 14) brings a painful rift, but Teo never exposes or betrays her. She thaws after Pell's backlog arrives. They fight side by side on Europa, Piq takes on extra dose to protect Teo, they confess in the tanker's medical bay, and in Chapter 24 they choose each other despite an uncertain future.

Teo and Amaya: grief turns to hope when Teo recognizes her sister's keying in the pulses. The flight recorder file proves Lagrange's own clause caused the crash. The sisters reunite on Europa, and the claim is reversed in Chapter 24.

Piq and Pell: light delay and the relay backlog make Pell read as ruthless. Twist 3 recasts him as a man answering stale reports. Resolved when Piq resigns, Pell apologizes, and Lagrange rewrites Clause 14(c).

The Bucket Brigade: Piq goes from hunting them to becoming their indispensable mass master. Hesper's martyr arc resolves when she chooses to stay and hold the depot pumps, and Lagrange's salvage funding secures the Brigade's amnesty.

Saar's crackdown: surveillance, the confiscated receiver, the interrogation, the cut fuel line and the corrupted navigation file. Resolved when Piq's impound seal outmaneuvers him and Rook detains him for a Compact inquiry using Piq's seal logs.

Rook and the missing mass: the full 340 tonnes is accounted for, 244 taken by the Brigade and 96 sublimated through the failed sunshade Rook hid. Resolved when she sides with Piq, repairs the shade and resigns.

Ur Station: framed as a threat through the war-risk purchase, the loitering tanker and Haddad's guarded protocol messages, Ur turns out to be running a parallel rescue (Twist 4). Resolved with a joint recovery and no war-risk claim ever triggered.

Cover collision and the cross-moon wedding: Piq's duplicate notary listing forces her to officiate Lucky and Ziva's wedding over a three-second delay. That same notary seal later powers the impound gambit, and the couple finally meet in person in Chapter 23.
Ballast the contraband cat: found as a 4.1 kg duct anomaly, the cat recurs as a comic interrupter and is formally entered into the Asgard ledger in Chapter 24.
The dose ledger: Teo's rigid limits clash with what the rescue demands. Resolved when she knowingly exceeds her own limit to save the crew and logs it honestly, accepting the review of her license.

outline.summary:
Weigh-In. Piq Varga rides the shuttle down into the Valhalla basin on Callisto. At Asgard Yard's mass intake she reads 1.3 kg over her 20 kg allowance because of the Lagrange Mutual Special Losses kit hidden inside her luggage. She keeps a straight face and talks her way through with bureaucratic fluency, declaring the hollow comms unit as 'audit reference masses' certified for calibrating depot scales. The bored weigh clerk logs them, taxes them, and asks her to sign in triplicate. Comedy comes from mass tariffs and Piq's weigh-master upbringing on a cycler ship.

At dose intake she meets Teodora 'Teo' Anand, the dose warden. Teo refuses Piq's request for a dosimeter waiver, quotes her sievert budget to three decimal places, and calls auditors and insurers 'the same species of vulture.' The hostility is immediate and charged. Piq catalogs Teo the way she catalogs cargo, and fails to make the total come out neutral.

During the final approach Piq notices frost on the sunward face of the ice depot, which is physically wrong. She files it away. [Sublimation clue.]

In her cramped quarters she reviews handler Augustin Pell's compressed briefing. The intercepted line 'throw before conjunction, no one will see it until it's done' reached Lagrange through a commercial intercept broker. Pell fears a weapon launch from the Sling or an engineered insurance fraud. Solar conjunction cuts her off in 38 days. [Hook 2 seed.]

She notes the low-g details of her new home: the slow arc of a dropped stylus, regolith grit in the door seal, Jupiter fixed and low through the frost. On her first night inside the depot ledger her reconciliation fails. Ending: 340 tonnes of water ice are missing.

The Ledger. Piq begins her genuine audit work.

A grumbling tug crew complains about water blankets, and she recites Lagrange's Clause 14(c), the dose clause, as gospel: minimum shielding water on any Europa-bound vessel, scaled by transit time. [Twist 2 clue.]

A chatty comms tech explains how traffic will run as conjunction nears. It routes through the Mars store-and-forward relay, which batches messages, reorders them by priority and size, deprioritizes large padded packets, and finally goes dark for 19 days. Piq pads all her covert reports to look like bulky routine audit uploads, and she notes the explanation only as a cover detail. [Twist 3 clue.]

Marek Saar, JDA head of security, introduces himself with a smile that audits her back and a reminder that Europa is a JDA-claimed exclusion zone.

Hesper Okafor-Lund, chief engineer, gives Piq a tour of the 40 km Sling. She talks with quiet pride about the slugs and the young crews she has trained.

Comedy: Piq discovers residents hiding mass everywhere, including contraband spices, an unlogged accordion and 'decorative' ballast bricks. Her sensor sweep flags a 4.1 kg anomaly in a ventilation duct. She crawls in expecting smuggled ice and finds Ballast, a contraband tabby. The cat steals her ration bar and vanishes in a slow low-g leap.

Ending: that night her covert receiver catches a faint pulse on a retired dosimetry maintenance band that no one should be using.

Pattern. Piq logs the pulses obsessively on tally sheets. Every 4.5 days they go silent for about 30 hours. She reads the gaps as a cabal's shift roster, with conspirators rotating off-duty, and starts cross-referencing them against depot crew schedules. She finds a partial correlation with Hesper's rotation, which she over-trusts. [Twist 1 clue.]

Cover collision comedy: Ibis Metrology, the firm behind her genuine credential, has also listed her as a registered notary. The station administrator's office cheerfully informs her that she is the only notary within 600,000 km. They ask her to officiate a cross-moon wedding between tug pilot Dov 'Lucky' Mbeki and Ziva Kalnins, a tanker pilot from Ur Station. Refusing would look suspicious. Director Ilse Rook signs off with brittle warmth and a nervous glance at the depot schedule.

Piq keeps running into Teo. They have a prickly exchange over Piq's dose logs, and Teo corrects her rounding.

At shift change Piq tails Hesper through service tunnels using a classic dead-reckoning surveillance pattern adapted to 0.126 g strides.

Ending: in a sealed hangar she sees a decommissioned tug, the Mule, being wrapped in hand-cut ice blocks, and realizes she has found where some of the ice went.

Mule. Piq stakes out the hangar from a maintenance crawlway.

She overhears Lucky, a nonstop talker who taps the hull three times for luck, complaining that 'Lagrange's water blankets cost me 300 meters per second' on every Europa job. He is fitting the Mule with shielding all the same. [Twist 2 clue.]

She skims JDA tracking from a public terminal. An Ur propellant tanker, the Steadfast Margin, is loitering in a Ganymede-Callisto transfer orbit, and JDA bulletins call it a provocation. Piq logs it as a possible buyer for a weapon throw. [Twist 4 clue.]

Comedy: a Brigade worker spots her, and a low-g pursuit follows through the hydroponics gallery. Piq overestimates her push-off, sails in a long helpless arc, and lands in a lettuce rack. She emerges wearing butterhead and has to explain herself to a gardener who insists on weighing the damaged lettuce for the incident report.

She slips back toward the hangar to photograph the Mule's reactor shielding.

Ending: Marek Saar steps out of the shadows and catches her there. Smiling, he says, 'Auditors who wander get audited.' Her dosimeter, which has been ticking up near the reactor, chirps on cue.

The Dome. Piq's dose has spiked from standing near the Mule's reactor. Teo summons her for a mandatory dose consultation. The scene is funny, prickly and charged:
- Teo interrogates every minute of Piq's day.
- Piq invents audit errands to explain the exposure.
- Teo dismantles each alibi with dose arithmetic but does not report her.

For reasons neither of them examines, Teo takes her to the viewing dome to recalibrate her badge against the background. Jupiter's banded light lies on the frost outside. Teo explains that Europa 'ducks behind the old man' every four and a half days and that the dosimeters sing differently when it does. She means it as a dose warden's folklore. [Twist 1 clue.]

Teo mentions her younger sister Amaya, an engineer lost with the tug Ninefold Grace fourteen months ago. Lagrange denied the claim. Teo's contempt for insurers now has a face and a grief behind it, and Piq hides her flinch.

Alone later, Piq notices a slow frequency drift in the pulses, a creeping rise and fall. She blames cheap hardware run by a careless cabal. [Twist 1 clue.]

Ending: a 49-minute-old order from Pell arrives. Identify the throw cabal, and treat the depot crew as hostile.

Vows. Comedy set piece: Piq officiates Lucky's wedding to Ziva over a live link to the Ur tanker.
- The three-second delay makes their vows overlap and collide.
- Ziva says 'I do' before the question has reached her.
- Lucky answers a question she never asked.
- The guests laugh on a delay.
- Piq improvises a turn-taking protocol borrowed from audit sign-offs.
- Ballast steals the wedding cake protein.
- Teo attends and almost smiles at Piq, which Piq notes as an unreconciled entry.

Pell's latest reply arrives mid-reception. It earnestly answers Piq's week-old question about how to log a cat as mass for her cover, with full actuarial gravity. [Twist 3 clue.]

Afterward Teo shows Piq Amaya's last dose log from the Ninefold Grace. It ends in an inexplicable spike that Lagrange's adjusters never explained. [Twist 2 clue.] They lean over the data together and nearly touch hands, then don't.

Piq digs through station budgets and finds that Director Rook cut the maintenance funding for the depot sunshade during the repricing year. [Sublimation clue.]

Rewatching the wedding feed, Piq sees that the Ur tanker is carrying far more propellant than any routine run needs. [Twist 4 clue.]

Ending: Hesper corners Piq in a corridor. 'What are you really weighing?'

Echo. [TWIST 1, misread signal.]

Piq stalls Hesper with a half-truth. Then, prompted by Teo's 'ducks behind the old man,' she overlays the pulses' 30-hour silences on Europa's occultations behind Jupiter as seen from Callisto. They match exactly. The drift is not cheap hardware but the Doppler shift of Europa's orbital motion.

The transmitter is on Europa. The cabal is no cabal. The Brigade has been listening, not coordinating. 'Throw before conjunction' looks like it may have meant a rescue, not a weapon.

Piq breaks cover far enough to bring the raw pulse logs to Teo, framing it as an anomaly an auditor stumbled on. Teo recognizes her own old dosimetry keying protocol, in her sister's hand. It is the private shorthand she taught Amaya as a teenager. Her armor cracks.

The two women decode through the night. A faint secondary modulation riding under the pulses resists every scheme they try and is left unexplained. [Hook 1 seed.]

Ending, the decoded text: FOUR ALIVE. REACTOR DRUM 60 DAYS. PLEASE.

Piq sends Lagrange a long, padded report: the Ninefold Grace crew is alive and there is no weapon cabal.

A stale message from Pell crosses it. Ur has bought war-risk cover over the JDA's claimed Europa zone, and Piq is ordered to stop any unlicensed launch by 'any means'. [Twist 4 clue. Hook 3 seed: the Compact may treat incursion into the zone as an act of war.]

Teo brings Piq to the Brigade. Hesper, Lucky and the hangar crew accept her as 'the auditor who can count.' Piq does not tell Teo or the Brigade that she works for Lagrange. Her lie is one of omission, and it is easy, which she notices and dislikes.

She reads Lagrange's own claim file on the Ninefold Grace. The denial rests on the pilot having 'deviated to a low-energy trajectory', which counts as pilot error. [Twist 2 clue.]

Re-examining the original intercepted fragment, she notices it was encoded with an Ur-standard codec, the wrong one for any Lagrange or JDA source. She cannot explain it. [Hook 2 seed.]

Ending: Saar decrees that every movement of ice on Asgard now needs a security countersignature, which strangles the Brigade's supply.

Comedy: Piq and Teo make a microgravity trip to an orbital tank farm to 'audit' propellant the Brigade can legally borrow.
- A propellant bladder breaks loose and tumbles.
- They wrestle a stuck valve together.
- Teo lectures on dose while upside down.
- They work as a team for the first time.

Pell's next message asks about the weapon cabal as though Piq's report never arrived. Her outbound queue shows 'ACK pending' on her reports. She dismisses both as Pell's terseness and relay lag. [Twist 3 clues.]

Residents complain about rising humidity in the depot corridors. [Sublimation clue.]

Over the covert link Amaya writes that 'the ice talks at night.' [Hook 1 seed.]

Lucky jokes, 'Ganymede's the cheap seats, but Ur would shoot us.' [Twist 4 clue.]

Piq builds the delta-v ledger for the Mule: Callisto to Europa, landing, ascent, return. Teo and Piq nearly kiss in an airlock and are interrupted when Ballast drops out of a duct between them.

Ending: the ledger shows the Mule will be 140 m/s short of returning to Callisto with survivors aboard. Moments later Saar confiscates the Brigade's receiver.

Clause. [TWIST 2, a consequence nobody predicted.]

Piq's covert receiver is now the only link between Callisto and Europa, and she becomes the Brigade's lifeline. She relays Teo's dose triage plan for a surface rescue to the survivors. The survivors transmit the Ninefold Grace's flight recorder file in slow packets.

Piq and Teo reconstruct the loss. Clause 14(c) required 18 tonnes of shielding water. That pushed the tug past its delta-v margin and forced the slow, low-energy path that lingered in Europa's plasma torus. Amaya's dose spike was real: a radiation burst latched up the flight computer, and the crew crash-landed.

The 'pilot error' that justified Lagrange's denial was caused by Lagrange's own rule, the clause Piq recited as gospel in Chapter 2. Lucky's 300 m/s complaint was the whole story in miniature.

Teo is incandescent with rage at the insurer, still not knowing Piq works for it. Piq's ledger of herself no longer balances.

Ending: Piq decides to tell her.

Commissioner Yusuf Haddad-Ferreira of Ur Station sends a stiff, protocol-heavy message to the dose warden. He asks for Europa surface dose protocols and proposes 'dose sharing' under an interagency framework. The JDA reads it as reconnaissance. [Twist 4 clue.]

Comedy: the JDA and Ur exchange formal notices of escalating politeness. 'Profound regret' escalates to 'most sincere and abiding regret', and Saar is forced to cosign increasingly florid diplomatic courtesies. JDA bulletins warn that any Ur landing would draw a Compact response. [Hook 3 seed.]

At the viewing dome, under Jupiter, Piq confesses that she is a Lagrange Special Losses adjuster sent to find a cabal, and that her reports go to the company that denied Amaya's claim.

Teo goes still, then precise and cold. She lists every conversation Piq was paid to have.

Ending: Teo walks away, saying, 'I won't burn you. I'm not you.'

Teo stays cold but professional. She keeps Piq's dose logs scrupulously and does not expose her to Saar or the Brigade. Each correct, distant interaction costs Piq more than an accusation would.

Saar has Piq detained and interrogates her. The scene is tense and has no humor:
- He has logged her transmissions on bands he cannot read.
- She uses the 100-minute round trip to Earth-Luna as an alibi. The transmissions are routine audit uploads to Ibis Metrology.
- He cannot verify them before the conjunction window closes.
- She uses procedure against him: her notary standing and audit chain of custody.

Saar shifts from threat to candor, which is more frightening.

Ending: Saar admits he signed the 'automated echo' ruling that dismissed the Ninefold Grace distress pulses, and says he cannot let the survivors exist.

Backlog. [TWIST 3, wrong assumption about time delay.]

Piq reaches the Mars relay operator directly, buying priority with a notary-seal override. The operator explains that her large padded reports have been stuck in the queue behind priority traffic all along. The padding that disguised her reports also buried them.

Every hard-line order from Pell was answering a world in which her last delivered report described a weapon cabal. The cat answer and the 'ACK pending' flags were the evidence.

Nine delayed messages from Pell arrive at once, out of order. The last says the survivors' existence has reached him, that Lagrange's salvage clause can fund the rescue, and 'help them, you'll be alone for 19 days.'

Piq realizes she has been arguing with a ghost of her own earlier report.

Teo reads Pell's message herself and begins to thaw. She concedes that Piq brought her the pulses at personal risk.

Ending: the conjunction blackout begins, and Saar locks down all launches from Asgard.

Seal. [Sublimation reveal, hidden physical constraint.]

Piq follows the frost, the sunshade budget cut and the humidity complaints. Her audit finds that 96 of the 340 missing tonnes sublimated off the depot because of the failed sunshade, which Rook concealed to avoid a rate hike. The Brigade took 244 tonnes. Piq uses the finding as leverage to bring Rook over.

Saar's team cuts the Mule's propellant feed.

Piq impounds the Mule under her mass-audit and notary seal, meaning it only as a delay. Under JDA statute, impounded assets fall outside security jurisdiction, so Saar's own protocol locks him out. The plan works for the wrong reason, a beat of dry comedy as Saar reads the statute twice. Rook quietly restores the feed under 'audit custody.'

Hesper, who planned to fly the rescue herself, gives up her martyrdom and stays to manually hold the depot pumps, which only she can do.

Ending: the launch window opens in nine hours, and the ledger is still 140 m/s short.

The transit runs through rising dose. There is no comedy in this chapter.

Teo calculates everyone's budget minute by minute and moves people around the shielding water. In the shielded cabin she and Piq share a quiet, intimate exchange about Amaya, about belonging, and about rules that never lied. Neither names what is between them.

Piq's cross-checking habit catches a corrupted Europa navigation file that Saar planted. They correct it by hand, but the margin is eaten. They land 2 km from the target.

The shielded crawler crosses chaos terrain under 5 Sv per day. They find the survivors in the ice:
- Captain Rhee;
- Wierzbicki;
- Oduya;
- Amaya.
The sisters reunite in a scene of restrained, devastating feeling.

The crevasse is closing. Amaya shows a hydrophone that has recorded structured periodic sounds that are not tidal cracking. [Hook 1 seed.]

Ending: with four survivors aboard, Piq's numbers show the Mule is too heavy to make the tanker rendezvous.

Jettison and rendezvous. There is no comedy until the docking succeeds.

Piq audits every kilogram aboard. She leaves behind her Lagrange comms unit, the hollow 'audit reference masses', her last tie to her job. Amaya keeps a 0.8 kg ice core sample, and Piq lets it stand on the ledger. The dead crewmembers return only as dog tags. Piq takes extra time on the EVA to cut away the ice blocks and stay outside longer, sparing Teo's dose by spending her own.

The burn comes up short. Ziva takes the Steadfast Margin deeper into the radiation field to meet them, and the rendezvous runs on a knife's edge.

The Mule docks. Only then does comedy return: Lucky and Ziva meet in person for the first time, with no delay. Nobody talks over anyone, and he still can't stop talking.

In the medical bay, both showing early symptoms of radiation sickness, Piq and Teo confess their love plainly.

Ending: the tanker sets course for Ur Station, with the dose readings still climbing on the monitors.

Resolution on Ur Station. The blackout ends, and Pell's message arrives:
- Lagrange reverses the Ninefold Grace denial, pays the claim and rewrites Clause 14(c).
- It funds the rescue as salvage, with legal amnesty for the Brigade.

On Callisto, Rook detains Saar for a Compact inquiry using Piq's seal logs, then resigns. The depot sunshade is repaired, and Hesper reports the pumps held.

The Ur-JDA war-risk claim is never triggered.

Piq resigns from Special Losses. Pell accepts with a rare unclipped apology.

Ballast is officially entered into the Asgard ledger as 'biological pest control, 4.1 kg'.

Lucky and Ziva settle on Ur. Amaya's crew is home.

Piq and Teo choose each other while their future stays uncertain:
- both carry elevated lifetime dose and blood counts that need watching;
- Teo's license is under review for exceeding her limits;
- Piq has no job and no home moon.
Teo logs her own overdose honestly. Piq does not reconcile the feeling; she lets it stand.

Deliberate trilogy hooks, left open on purpose:
(1) Amaya's ice core and the hydrophone recordings of structured periodic sound beneath the ice remain unexplained.
(2) On the final page an unsigned message arrives on the old dosimetry band: 'Well counted.'
(3) The Compact has dispatched the enforcement vessel Integrity, 26 months out, naming Piq a witness.

== STATUS ==
Ch18 delivered the transit, the arrival on Ur, the whole planned Ch19-24 resolution, all three hooks and the final 'Well counted' line. The story has reached its ending; the planned chapters 19-24 were absorbed into Ch18. If revision is ever needed, see the CONTINUITY DISCREPANCIES section below.

== CH18 FACTS (canon) ==

TRANSIT (D31-D33)
- Piq's sickness began at 2140 D31. Emesis times: 2140, 2212, 2251, 2340, 0108, 0241.
- Notebook page headed 'SELF'.
- Margin rolled its tankage toward the belts. The readout fell from 6.4 to 4.9, then 0.6 by 0300, then 0.18 at 0500 D33.
- Teodorescu is silent and communicates with laminated cards: PLEASE BE STILL, NO, BETTER (with a '?' added in pen).
- Bloods at 0810 D32: Piq's lymphocytes 1.4, Teo's 1.6. Counts daily, then weekly, then for life.
- Piq: 'I'd like it to be you.' Teo: 'Ask me when you can keep breakfast down.'
- Teo's pencil stub came through everything, unweighed (about 12 g).
- Rhee in the 'quiet room' by the galley: lymphocytes 0.1*, platelets 40, on oxygen and a line. Oduya keeps a foot through a floor strap and a hand on his arm. Teo told him she did not know if he would live.
- Rhee asked Piq to say Kat Sefton's name to Lagrange, 'not the arithmetic.' She promised.
- Lucky had been married 26 days and together in person for 19 h, with no privacy. Priit, the loadmaster, keeps trying to weigh him.
- The Ur manifest rejected the survivors and suggested 'Rhee, J., deceased'. Piq resolved it:
  - port of embarkation entered as 61.2 S, R-K4;
  - correction of record filed under her Ibis seal: Rhee, Wierzbicki, Oduya and Anand witnessed alive;
  - Sefton, Bui and Lachance confirmed deceased, remains in situ, tags retained.
- Margin crew doses against the 150 mSv waiver: Sabri 131, Priit 118, Halvorsen 144, Teodorescu 152, Kalnins 171.
  - Ziva and Teodorescu are over. Ziva: 'It is not your column.'
  - Piq keeps a 'PAID BY' page listing the five names. Ziva: 'You may keep that page. You may not settle it.'
- Ziva wears Lucky's brass fish on a cord at her collar.
- The core is in Margin's cold locker, labelled 'SAMPLE, GEOLOGICAL (?), 0.79 KG, OWNER ANAND A., DO NOT OPEN'.
- The sisters' talk (Piq present):
  - Teo had closed Amaya's dose record in pencil after the ruling.
  - Amaya told her to reopen it.
  - Amaya used the six-by-six grid hoping Teo would hear.
  - Piq said she is resigning. Amaya broke down and Teo held her.

ARRIVAL AND SAAR
- Ur sighted at 0710 D33.
- Saar's notice, timestamped D32 1802 and held 13 h in the Authority queue:
  - it called the survivors deceased and 'contents';
  - it demanded the return of the Mule, its contents and Varga.
  - Piq struck 'contents' and wrote 'Persons. 7. Fixed.'
- Rook's message, sent 0719 D33:
  - at 0540 D33 Saar was relieved and DETAINED pending a Compact inquiry;
  - the grounds were the Ibis seal logs: attempted entry, the cut feed, and the upload of nav survey 2214.7c under his credential;
  - the reservation of rights against Ur is withdrawn and the persons are recognised as living;
  - postscript: 'Tell the auditor her seal held.'
- Haddad met them at mast two and bowed to each person. Ur 'houses' auditors, 'pending'.

ON UR
- The clinic sits under the crater wall; Teo rates its dose 'rude but survivable'.
- Rhee: growth factors; sat up day 6, broth day 9. Oduya first slept day 12.
- Piq's lymphocytes bottomed at 0.9 on day 11, then rose to 1.1 at D52. Teo corrected her graph's axis.
- Hesper, day 3:
  - held the pumps by manual valve cycling for 61 h;
  - Rook produced a spare membrane;
  - the sunshade was back up and the frost gone;
  - 96 t lost for good, no more.
  - On the Brigade's ice: '244 we spent.'
- Rook resigned in four lines. On her last day she signed the Ballast entry: 'biological pest control, 4.1 kg, undeclared, now declared, duty waived for service in the ventilation system'. Piq countersigned it. Hesper sent a photo of Ballast on a warm duct.
- Lucky and Ziva: given quarters on day 9, ring corridor, level 3, with a door and a lock (Priit has a key). Lucky got Ur short-haul tug work, Ganymede to the tank farms. They are buying a table, 7.2 kg, and Piq is invited to dinner. Lucky is '4% angry'.

RELAY AND PELL
- The relay returned at 0311 D52 Ur time.
- Pell's packet (PRIORITY, ALL ROUTES):
  - he says he received her reports in full on D41 'by relay drain before the blackout closed';
  - claim 1146 denial reversed; Sefton named and cleared; paid in full with interest;
  - Clause 14(c) withdrawn; a replacement is to weigh shielding against transit time, with Piq implied as drafter;
  - salvage under Clause 31, Society-funded; the diverted ice is a salvage expense; Brigade amnesty, signed by Rook;
  - Ur war-risk claim not triggered: 'No one is at war';
  - a full, unqualified apology, expecting her resignation.
- Piq's resignation, 5 lines: accepts the apology and asks that the claim record state Sefton held the Grace by hand and was the best pilot on file.
- Round trip 101 min. Pell's unclipped reply at 0834: '...I hope wherever you go next they understand what they've got.'

TEO
- Licence suspended pending review, with pay. Notice from the Asgard dose board.
- In ink, on printed ledger pages:
  - Amaya's page: 'REOPENED. 2214 D52. Cumulative 1.21 Sv, surface interval excluded... Subject living.'
  - Her own page: 'ANAND, T. Europa surface and transit, D29-D32. 612 mSv. Exceeds emergency limit by 362 mSv. Knowing and voluntary. Self-reported.'
- 'It's the only rule that never lied to me.'
- Piq: 'Stay with me. Wherever that turns out to be. I don't know the numbers yet.' Teo: 'I'll tell you when I know them. I won't make them nicer.' Her hand was on Piq's wrist, not counting.
- Piq's page 'T. ANAND', with owed / paid / difference columns, left empty and unreconciled.

HOOK 1, D54
- The hydrophone playback in Rhee's room.
- Tidal signals run on an 85 h clock.
- The anomaly:
  - a deep, pitched pulse pattern: 3, pause, 4, pause, 3;
  - blocks of about 40 min that drift against the orbit;
  - blocks recur every few days, slightly altered.
- Amaya claims nothing: 'can't make it into anything else.'
- The core was cut where the sound was loudest. It remains unopened.
- Rhee: 'it was there before we were.'

HOOK 3, D56
- Compact Office of Inquiry: Integrity dispatched, about 26 months out.
- Witnesses: Haddad-Ferreira, Kalnins, Anand T., Varga.
- Haddad again: 'The codec was ours. The hand was not.' Someone 'knew you would count.'

HOOK 2, night of D56, 0217
- Teo's old Asgard warden dosimeter (with the cartoon-sun sticker) chirped a receive tone on the dosimetry band.
- The message came in the six-by-six grid, in an unknown hand, with no header.
- Strength: too strong for Europa, too faint for Ur, no Doppler.
- It read WELL COUNTED. Amaya was asleep and her slate dark.
- Piq reached for the notebook. END.

- Everyone recovered lives on Ur.
- Saar detained. Rook resigned. Hesper and the Brigade amnestied. Sunshade repaired.
- Piq resigned, with no job, witness status, and Ibis seal standing in doubt.
